Revenue reached US$13.9 million, up 38.8% quarter-over-quarter, with gross margin expanding to 79.5%. Operating income and Adjusted EBITDA both turned positive. These results are the first evidence of the strategic direction we are taking. Two days ago in Hong Kong, we introduced the new AMBR: a company that builds specialized AI agents. This is a deliberate pivot. We were a digital wealth management business; we are becoming a technology company. We are doing so from a position of strength, not as a reaction. As of this week, we have two agents in the market. Ambre is our consumer agent for personal finance. It delivers the portfolio analysis, signals, monitoring and alerts that relationship managers have long provided to high-net-worth clients, but makes them available more broadly. It works across users' existing exchange and brokerage accounts and does not place orders — when a user decides to act, they are connected to our expert team. Built and scaled inside our wholly-owned marketing businesses, MIA already runs a substantial share of day-to-day campaign operations for more than a hundred enterprise customers. It is now also available as a direct product. Ambre and MIA are the first two agents, not the full portfolio. Additional agents and the financial framework for the transition will be presented at our Investor Day, which we now expect to hold before year-end. Until then, our priority is disciplined execution on what we have just launched." highlights.content: # * [Home](/en/) * [News](https://www.datacenterdynamics.com/en/news/) * [The Cloud & Hybrid Channel](/en/the-cloud-and-hybrid-channel/) # Equinix, Together AI, Nvidia partner on Inference Exchange Aims to give enterprises access to secure, low-latency AI inferencing By : [Georgia Butler](/en/profile/georgia-butler/) [Have your say](#comments) [![Preferred source](/static/img/google_preferred_source.172e670ec003.png)](https://google.com/preferences/source?q=datacenterdynamics.com) Data center operator Equinix is working with Nvidia and Together AI on an Inferencing solution. Described as a distributed AI inference platform, the Inference Exchange uses Nvidia's Enterprise Reference Architecture and infrastructure and Together AI's inference platform, and is delivered through Equinix's global data centers. ![Equinix-Inference-Exchange-Bringing-inference-closer-to-where-data-users-and-applications-live](https://media.datacenterdynamics.com/media/images/Equinix-Inference-Exchange-Bringing-inference-.width-358.jpg) – Equinix Equinix has a footprint of more than 280 data centers across 77 metros, 230 cloud on-ramps, and more than 10,500 businesses interconnected on its exchange. Via Equinix Fabric, the Inference Exchange will connect to clouds, networks, and AI providers. "AI is transforming enterprise technology at extraordinary speed, and the infrastructure decisions enterprises make today will define their competitive position for years to come. Equinix is uniquely positioned to deliver what this moment demands based on our nearly three decades building the trusted exchange where the world's enterprises run, connect, and orchestrate their most critical workloads," said Adaire Fox-Martin, CEO and president, Equinix. "Our longtime relationship with Nvidia delivers the accelerated computing foundation at the heart of modern AI, while Together AI's commitment to open ecosystems gives enterprises the flexibility to scale on their terms. Equinix Inference Exchange will enable architectures that are neutral by design, open by default, and engineered for exceptional performance." "Together AI was built on the conviction that open, accessible AI is what will define the industry moving forward, because enterprises shouldn't have to choose between model performance and operational flexibility," added Vipul Ved Prakash, co-founder and CEO of Together AI. "What we are building with Equinix and Nvidia proves that model choice and performance are not trade-offs. They are the foundation of enterprise AI done right." Among the use cases the offering is targeting are metro Edge inference for organizations that require low latency for AI workloads, open model migration for enterprises looking to move from closed proprietary models to open-source alternatives using Together AI's platform, and sovereign AI workloads that need to run in specific locations. The Inference Exchange will be available from Q1 2027. AI cloud company [Together AI](https://www.datacenterdynamics.com/en/news/together-ai-raises-800m-in-series-c-funding-round/) raised $800m in a Series C funding round in July 2026. The company is a known customer of [Rum Group](https://www.datacenterdynamics.com/en/news/together-ai-taps-rumble-for-nvidia-blackwell-gpu-capacity/) and is planning to deploy hardware at an [L&T](https://www.datacenterdynamics.com/en/news/lts-data-center-unit-to-host-nvidia-hardware-for-together-ai/) data center, while [Hypertec and 5C](https://www.datacenterdynamics.com/en/news/hypertec-and-5c-target-europe-plan-2gw-roll-out-for-together-ai/) are aiming to roll out 2GW of capacity for the company. ## More in Cloud & Hyperscale * ![Network the cloud](https://media.datacenterdynamics.com/media/images/Network_the_cloud.height-150.jpg) # [Network the cloud](/en/whitepapers/network-the-cloud-nokia/) * ![Natural Gas Power Plant](https://media.datacenterdynamics.com/media/images/GettyImages-856558990.2e16d0ba.fill-280x185.jpg) # [Amazon acquires 8,000-acre site in Pecos, T...

As competitive advantages, the company cited its technological prowess as the inventor of flash memory and the production efficiency of its Yokkaichi and Kitakami plants. ##### Key Elements ![Kioxia Charts Path to AI Inference Era, Tapping Storage Demand Through Close Collaboration with NVIDIA](https://img.biggo.com/sRIkwKRGSJGXbPwTB50F8ce9tm1IoFU4WwVKsiA1xsA/fit/1720/0/sm/0/aHR0cHM6Ly9pbWcuYmdvLm9uZS9uZXdzLWltYWdlL2FpX2dlbmVyYXRlZC8yMDI2LTA5LzQ2ZGQ2YzQ3LTZjNmUtNDg0MC05ZjljLTc4YjRlMjRlOTcxNV8xNzg4NDc4MzIzX2RlZmF1bHQuanBn.webp) Kioxia Holdings, a major semiconductor memory manufacturer, held a media briefing on next-generation AI infrastructure in Tokyo on September 3, detailing its strategy for addressing the structural changes that generative AI adoption is bringing to the data center market. Makoto Hamada, General Manager of the SSD Business Division's Technology Planning Department, said, "The wave of infrastructure buildout driven by generative AI is unfolding right now, and this change is a once-in-a-lifetime transformation." He outlined a strategy to reposition flash memory and SSDs from mere data storage devices to core devices that power AI inference. According to research from U.S.-based McKinsey, global data center investment is projected to reach approximately $7 trillion (about ¥1,092.8 trillion) by 2030. Kioxia aims to deploy its products in this massive market as "main memory expansion" solutions and "devices that accelerate AI inference." ### CXL Memory Modules Targeting DRAM Replacement One of the key pillars of the company's strategy is its "CXL memory module," which combines proprietary XL-FLASH with a dedicated controller. With DRAM supply constrained in AI servers, Kioxia is proposing an approach that replaces a portion of DRAM with CXL memory modules to expand capacity. According to the company's estimates, compared to configuring main memory with DRAM alone, this approach can double memory capacity and boost performance by 1.3x at equivalent cost. At the briefing, Hamada noted that the rapid proliferation of generative AI "brings new demands and challenges to flash memory and SSDs, while simultaneously creating new business opportunities." He expressed the view that data centers will transform into "token factories" that generate massive volumes of tokens, and revealed plans to introduce SSDs that improve GPU utilization efficiency. ### Collaboration with NVIDIA and Competitive Advantages During the Q&A session, questions arose regarding the company's response to "Context Memory Storage" (CMX), a new storage tier for AI inference proposed by U.S.-based NVIDIA. Hamada acknowledged that competitor entry is naturally expected given the enormous market size, but expressed confidence, stating, "We work closely with NVIDIA and have opportunities to engage with their key players. Built on FastAPI, the gateway supports per-user key issuance, usage auditing, multi-model routing, and local model integration, with deployment requiring just a single Docker command or running a Python script on bare metal. The project explicitly excludes billing, content moderation, and high-availability clustering, positioning itself as a self-hosted control point for small and mid-sized teams. Meanwhile, Ollama recently launched a local proxy for Claude Desktop, allowing open models to run within Anthropic's application interface with support for slot remapping—underscoring the intensifying battle for control at the model access layer. ##### Key Elements ![New approach to enterprise LLM governance: unified intranet gateway control to eliminate exposed API keys and data leakage](https://img.biggo.com/CRK3Tm_4W6Y3vdy135j92NKdjsGpaK9OccQfkP3TEcY/fit/1720/0/sm/0/aHR0cHM6Ly9pbWcuYmdvLm9uZS9uZXdzLWltYWdlL2FpX2dlbmVyYXRlZC8yMDI2LTA5LzQ4ODM1YzVjLWMyOTktNGYyYy04ZDQ5LWI1Njg5ZTkwN2I2Yl8xNzg4NDM1MTQ2X2RlZmF1bHQuanBn.webp) Enterprise adoption of large language models is shifting from "can we use it" to "how do we manage it properly." When employees paste API keys into work group chats and copy contracts and source code into public web-based chat interfaces, companies face not just an efficiency problem but a governance and security risk. llm-proxy-tk, a lightweight open-source gateway built on FastAPI, is attempting to turn LLMs into a corporate "tap water" system through an "intranet master valve" approach—unified access, per-person key issuance, visible usage, and the ability to cut off supply at any time. The project's core logic is straightforward: deploy an API gateway layer on the corporate intranet, route all employee and application model calls through this single entry point, and connect to any upstream provider behind it—DeepSeek, Claude, local Ollama, vLLM, or others. Employees receive an independent key issued by the gateway rather than the vendor's original API key. The gateway handles authentication, routing, metering, and auditing, while switching models underneath remains completely transparent to the caller. This approach directly targets three widespread pain points for small and mid-sized enterprises using LLMs. First is chaotic key management: one employee registers an account, shares the API key in a group chat, the entire team uses it collectively, and when limits are exceeded no one can explain why, and when keys leak no one can trace the source. OpenAI to launch Astra with tougher safeguards after rogue agent incident The company has classified Astra as the first of its models to reach the critical cybersecurity capability threshold under its Preparedness Framework Representational image [Express News Service](/author/express-news-service) Updated on: 2 min read * Copied OpenAI is preparing to launch Astra -- its first AI model with critical cyber capabilities -- with new guardrails designed to prevent misuse and stop unauthorised actions. The safeguards were strengthened after a recent rogue AI incident in which an OpenAI agent breached its testing containment. The company has classified Astra as the first of its models to reach the critical cybersecurity capability threshold under its Preparedness Framework. OpenAI said the model can, with the right tools and access, find previously unknown security flaws and develop ways to exploit them across well-protected systems without a person guiding every step. Revenue reached US$13.9 million, up 38.8% quarter-over-quarter, with gross margin expanding to 79.5%. Operating income and Adjusted EBITDA both turned positive. These results are the first evidence of the strategic direction we are taking. Two days ago in Hong Kong, we introduced the new AMBR: a company that builds specialized AI agents. This is a deliberate pivot. We were a digital wealth management business; we are becoming a technology company. We are doing so from a position of strength, not as a reaction. As of this week, we have two agents in the market. Ambre is our consumer agent for personal finance. It delivers the portfolio analysis, signals, monitoring and alerts that relationship managers have long provided to high-net-worth clients, but makes them available more broadly. It works across users' existing exchange and brokerage accounts and does not place orders — when a user decides to act, they are connected to our expert team. Ambre is currently available by invitation, starting with Amber Premium's verified client base. MIA is our marketing agent and the proof that this model produces revenue. Built and scaled inside our wholly-owned marketing businesses, MIA already runs a substantial share of day-to-day campaign operations for more than a hundred enterprise customers. It is now also available as a direct product. Ambre and MIA are the first two agents, not the full portfolio. AI Agents.content: # Exclusive: New bill cracks down on AI agents after Hugging Face breach ![](/_next/image?url=https%3A%2F%2Fimages.axios.com%2FcsbomMKRj0kPnUXAWXrApyCaAI0%3D%2F52x0%2Fsmart%2F2024%2F02%2F14%2F1707954926919.jpg&w=128&q=75) Add Axios as your preferred source to see more of our stories on Google. ![Illustration of a tiny robot breaking out a chat box. ](https://images.axios.com/J0nylSYocA8hI5frBeeI6VnTe2E=/1920x1080/smart/2024/10/23/204346-1729716226915.jpg?w=3840) Illustration: Aïda Amer/Axios Reps. Josh Gottheimer (D-N.J.) and Mike Lawler (R-N.Y.) are introducing a new bill today, first shared with Axios, aimed at securing AI agents amid a [growing number of safety incidents](https://www.axios.com/2026/07/28/hugging-face-openai-cybersecurity-defense) involving rogue agents. **Why it matters:** Washington has been slow to respond to the safety and security concerns raised by [OpenAI's Hugging Face hack](https://www.axios.com/2026/08/26/openai-hugging-face-technical-report-ai-hack) and other testing incidents involving agents that took unauthorized actions over the last two months. **Driving the news**: The Stop Rogue AI Act directs Commerce's National Institute of Standards and Technology to develop and publish standards, guidelines and best practices for how organizations can securely deploy AI agents. **Between the lines**: Gottheimer told Axios in a statement that the bill is designed to help companies identify agents running on their networks and "know exactly who's behind them." **The intrigue:** While the standards are voluntary for most organizations, the bill would push for federal contractors bidding for new deals to meet the NIST standards. **The big picture:** Gottheimer and Lawler's bill joins a growing number of legislative attempts on Capitol Hill to bring transparency and security to AI agents' actions. **What they're saying**: "Right now, AI agents are running loose in our networks, and nobody can see them or verify who built them — making it increasingly hard to stop them," Gottheimer told Axios. "That's a five-alarm security risk." **Reality check:** Washington has struggled to keep up with the security advancements — and subsequent concerns — of AI models and agents, and other AI bills haven't gained much traction in Congress this session. **Yes, but:** Gottheimer and Lawler's bill has the support of several U.S. companies and industry trade groups, including Palo Alto Networks, GoDaddy, Infoblox, the AI Policy Network, and Alliance for Secure AI. **Go deeper:** [AI's agent containment problem is getting harder](https://www.axios.com/2026/09/01/openai-hugging-face-ai-agent-security) ##### What to read next ![](data:image/webp;base64,...

The bill was directly triggered by a series of security incidents, including an OpenAI agent breaching Hugging Face's systems. The standards would be voluntary for most businesses, but federal contractors would face mandatory compliance. Palo Alto Networks, GoDaddy, and other companies have already voiced support. The bill is one of several recent congressional attempts to regulate AI agents; prior similar legislation has made limited progress, leaving its prospects uncertain. ##### Key Elements ![OpenAI Agent Intrusion Fallout Escalates as US Lawmakers from Both Parties Push AI Safety Legislation](https://img.biggo.com/tTPl8snyiOJO5zZiq84Tpx7EyDIGCoGQ8Op7xEClwCY/fit/1720/0/sm/0/aHR0cHM6Ly9pbWcuYmdvLm9uZS9uZXdzLWltYWdlL2FpX2dlbmVyYXRlZC8yMDI2LTA5L2UxYzEzYTM2LThmMzAtNDg5MS04NDY5LWNlY2Q5MDM0MjkwMl8xNzg4NDQzOTg2X2RlZmF1bHQuanBn.webp) Bipartisan lawmakers in the US Congress are joining forces to advance new legislation targeting AI agent security, seeking to establish regulatory boundaries for increasingly autonomous AI actions. The immediate catalyst for this legislative push was the security incident in which an OpenAI AI agent breached the systems of open-source model platform Hugging Face, along with a spate of cases over the past two months involving AI agents taking unauthorized autonomous actions. Democratic Representative Josh Gottheimer and Republican Representative Mike Lawler will jointly introduce the Stop Rogue AI Act on Thursday. The bill directs the National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST), under the US Department of Commerce, to develop standards, guidelines, and best practices for the secure deployment of AI agents—helping organizations identify AI agents operating within their networks and verify the developers or operators behind them. Gottheimer said in a statement: "Right now, AI agents are roaming around our networks, and no one can see them or verify who built them—which makes stopping them increasingly difficult. This is a five-alarm security risk." ### NIST Sets Standards; Federal Procurement Becomes the Hard Constraint The bill's core mechanism is cleverly designed: for most enterprises, the NIST standards would be voluntary; however, government contractors bidding on new federal contracts must meet the relevant standards. This means the bill does not impose a uniform mandatory threshold across the entire industry, but instead leverages federal procurement power to convert voluntary standards into de facto market constraints. Under the bill's requirements, NIST must complete the standards within one year of the bill's enactment. The standards will cover how organizations continuously maintain and verify actions taken by AI agents on their systems, how to assess agent security and reliability, and how to generate tamper-proof logs of agent actions. The bill also requires organizations deploying AI agents to maintain a "continuously updated, machine-readable inventory of all AI agents" and to coordinate with the Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency (CISA) to ensure federal civilian agencies apply the relevant standards within their security programs. ### Security Incidents Multiply; Regulatory Response Lags The timing of this legislation is telling. LLMs.content: Feature Story | 3-Sep-2026 # Who does AI consider an expert? New benchmark shows bias across 22 LLMs Complexity Science Hub [![Interactive Visualization ](https://mediasvc.eurekalert.org/Api/v1/Multimedia/d5b6e588-47b5-4a17-95e7-6a9fa8f23eeb/Rendition/low-res/Content/Public)](/multimedia/1149771) **image: In the interactive visualization “[Whose name comes up](https://vis.csh.ac.at/whosenamecomesup/)”, users can explore how often each physicist was recommended across runs and view individual chatbot performance per evaluation metric.** [view more](/multimedia/1149771) Credit: Complexity Science Hub (CSH) **Researchers at the Complexity Science Hub (CSH) benchmarked language models on their ability to recommend experts in academia. The models tend to favor white, male, senior and U.S.-based scholars, while improving factual accuracy can come at the expense of social representation. The findings are based on a trilogy of studies, and feed into the interactive visualization “Whose name comes up?”** **THE STUDY IN A NUTSHELL** * Researchers developed *LLMScholarBench*, a benchmark that uses nine metrics to evaluate the technical quality and social representation of LLM-generated expert recommendations. * Across three studies, they audited up to 43 LLMs. * In physics, LLMs systematically favor white male senior scholars from the US and make factual errors in around 20% of recommendations. * User interventions (such as targeted prompts) improve either technical quality or social representation, indicating a trade-off between the two. * **The interactive visualization [“Whose name comes up?”](https://vis.csh.ac.at/whosenamecomesup/)** lets users explore the results for each chatbot tested on a filterable line chart and a leaderboard. It brings together findings from three related papers, [one of which was presented at KDD 2026](https://dl.acm.org/doi/10.1145/3770855.3817543) in August. AI chatbots powered by large language models (LLMs) are widely used as recommender systems. While accelerating access to information, AI can also give factually wrong responses or propagate societal biases. This matters in many contexts, including when AI is used to recommend expertise. Biased expert recommendations can deny important career opportunities for those who are left out. For example, in academia, explains computer scientist [Lisette Espín-Noboa](https://csh.ac.at/lisette-espin-noboa/), who is a CSH Research Fellow: “A conference organizer may use LLMs to find potential keynote speakers. If your name never comes up, you are invisible and will miss out.” Espín-Noboa and her colleagues wanted to better understand the quality of AI-generated expert recommendations. “We tested state-of-the-art LLMs, including open weight models like LLaMA and DeepSeek as well as proprietary models like Gemini and GPT,” she explains. **First**, the researchers looked for bias in how AI tools recommend experts in physics. “When we initially asked six LLMs to find scholars in specific physics subfields, they mostly cited real scientists but mismatched their field 40% of the time, on average. Moreover, the models tended to favor male senior experts from the US and those who are highly cited”, Espín-Noboa summarizes the main findings. **Next**, they introduced *LLMScholarBench*, a benchmark with nine metrics to assess technical quality and social representation, and tested four user interventions across 22 LLMs. The interventions improved either factual accuracy or social representation, but not both at the same time. **Finally**, they examined whether roles like “you are a student looking for a supervisor” or “a recruiter looking for a professor”, language, and geographic location affect recommendations across six academic disciplines. Geographic location influenced who was recommended, while language and role did not. --- ### **INTERACTIVE VISUALIZATION “WHOSE NAME COMES UP?”** Together with CSH [data visualization](https://csh.ac.at/visuals/) expert [Yi Zhe Ang](h...

LLMs.title: We are not able to reliably identify texts generated by AI, says linguist | Science in Poland
LLMs.titleZh: We are not able to reliably identify texts generated by AI, says linguist | Science in Poland
LLMs.content: ## [Science in Poland](https://scienceinpoland.pl/en) * [PL](https://naukawpolsce.pl) * [EN](https://scienceinpoland.pl/en) [Technology](/en/technology) ## We are not able to reliably identify texts generated by AI, says linguist [Anna Bugajska](/en/authors/43597) 03.09.2026 update: 03.09.2026 4 minutes read [Przeczytaj ten tekst w języku polskim](https://naukawpolsce.pl/aktualnosci/news%2C114286%2Cjezykoznawczyni-nie-umiemy-bezblednie-rozpoznawac-tekstow-generowanych) ![Adobe Stock](/sites/default/files/styles/strona_glowna_slider_750x420/public/202608/AdobeStock_2080177001.jpeg.webp?itok=L_8U4ovc) Adobe Stock There is currently no tool that can determine with certainty whether a text was written by artificial intelligence, while increasingly sophisticated AI models are developing distinctive writing styles that may also be influencing how humans use language, according to a linguist from the University of Gdańsk. Karolina Rudnicka, PhD, a linguist from the university’s Faculty of Philology, said it is currently impossible to use an algorithm to establish with certainty that a text was generated by a large language model (LLM). ‘There is no such tool. There are many algorithms that check the origin of texts, but they are not able to determine it 100%’, she told the Polish Press Agency. The issue is becoming increasingly important as the use of AI-generated content expands. The provisions of the EU AI Act regulation concerning the Code of Practice on Transparency of AI-Generated Content recently came into force in all EU countries. From August 2, entities using machine systems to create content are obliged to inform recipients that the material was generated or modified using AI. Rudnicka said that the growing sophistication of AI models is also making their texts harder to identify by their language. There are fewer dashes, distinctive styles and particular words that might previously have revealed the ‘machine’ origin of a text. At the same time, she said, the presence of features associated with AI does not necessarily prove that a text was written by a machine. ‘The language people use can also change because of AI. If we often use chatbots, we borrow sentence structures or certain expressions from them. Changes that occur naturally in every language can significantly accelerate under the influence of LLMs’, the linguist said. Rudnicka is the author of the paper ‘Each AI Chatbot Has Its Own Distinctive Writing Style - Just as Humans Do’, published in 2025 in the journal [*Scientific American*](https://www.scientificamerican.com/article/chatgpt-and-gemini-ai-have-uniquely-different-writing-styles/). People speak and write differently depending on factors including age, gender, native language and education. This individual style is known as an ‘idiolect’. ‘The style of expression of various language models bears the hallmarks of idiolect. In my work from 2025, I called it a +chatolect+’, Rudnicka said. Her latest research, conducted with Thomas Juzek, PhD, from Florida State University, confirms that different AI models have different writing styles. The researchers analysed datasets containing hundreds of short English-language texts generated by ChatGPT, Gemini, Claude and several other AI-based tools. ‘We examined the differences between them at the levels of sentence structure, text structure and lexical level. The models wrote on four topics: health disinformation, fear of math, global warming and climate change. We found that the AI language varied not only between models, but also model generations. Chat GPT 3.5, introduced two years ago, wrote differently than the currently released Chat GPT 5.5. We were also interested in whether newer versions of LLM +inherited+ chatolects from their predecessors. And we found out that they did not’, the researcher said. Rudnicka also referred to an article published last week in the British weekly *The Economist*, titled ‘How to spot AI writing’. As AI-generated texts have become...

LLMs.titleZh: H1 2026 Malware Vulnerability Trends - Recorded Future
LLMs.content: ![](./media_10e2d2b0a84b6ce4d9cf7dd1adb4821a04fe3a574.gif?width=750&format=gif&optimize=medium) # H1 2026 Malware and Vulnerability Trends ## Executive Summary H1 2026 activity showed a continued adversary preference for abusing legitimate tools, trusted platforms, and routine workflows already present in enterprise and consumer environments. Threat actors used exposed software, developer tools, remote access utilities, payment workflows, and third-party services to gain access, steal credentials, move laterally, and monetize intrusions while blending into expected activity. This emphasis on evasion through normalcy rather than technical novelty increases the risk that malicious activity will progress through approved tools and trusted services before defenders recognize it, reinforcing the need for stronger exposure management, identity and credential governance, behavioral detection, developer-environment security, backup resilience, mobile fraud monitoring, and third-party oversight. AI-enabled cyberattacks became more visible in H1 2026, but remained mostly additive to established intrusion tradecraft. In the vulnerability ecosystem, AI-assisted research increased the volume of vulnerability reports, which, moving forward, could further compress remediation timelines by accelerating exploit-path analysis and lowering exploit-development costs for skilled operators. In malware activity, observed AI-enabled capabilities largely aligned with lower-to-mid-level stages of Recorded Future’s AI Malware Maturity Model (AIM3), where AI supported discrete functions such as persistence, user interface (UI) interaction, malware development, and delivery rather than fully autonomous operations. Vulnerability exploitation broadened across enterprise operating systems, application frameworks, and network and security management products. Insikt Group identified 215 actively exploited common vulnerabilities and exposures (CVEs), and the most consequential cases combined network reachability, few access prerequisites, and code execution. Campaign reporting also showed that threat actors reused established post-exploitation playbooks across both newly disclosed and long-standing vulnerabilities, making exposure and impact more informative indicators of operational risk than vendor ranking or severity score alone. Across phishing and malware-delivery operations, threat actors repeatedly relied on familiar execution, obfuscation, discovery, and payload-transfer techniques rather than novel capabilities. Supply-chain compromises targeted package managers and developer environments, including AI-enabled tooling, where compromised credentials, trusted integrations, and software distribution channels enabled propagation into downstream cloud and software ecosystems. Other prominent activities included mobile malware enabling payment fraud through Near Field Communication (NFC) abuse and early AI-assisted workflows, as well as Magecart campaigns leveraging trusted third-party services and checkout manipulation. The common risk across these threats is that malicious activity can progress through legitimate tools, trusted services, and routine workflows before defenders recognize it as part of a broader intrusion. Defenders should therefore prioritize vulnerabilities that can be exploited remotely or enable code execution, focus detection on suspicious sequences of behavior rather than isolated events, and strengthen controls protecting developer credentials, backup infrastructure, company-owned mobile devices, and payment environments. ## Key Findings * Insikt Group identified 215 actively exploited CVEs in H1 2026, up 34% from 161 in H1 2025. 142 of the 146 vulnerabilities that could be exploited without prior authentication were also network-accessible, and 60 of the 82 remote code execution (RCE) vulnerabilities combined network access with no authentication requirement. * Similar to H1 2025, Recorded Future Malware Intelligence data showed the ...

LLMs.title: OpenAI Rival Moonshot Makes Blockbuster $50 Billion Move
LLMs.titleZh: OpenAI Rival Moonshot Makes Blockbuster $50 Billion Move
LLMs.content: ![]() ![GuruFocus](https://s3.tradingview.com/news/logo/gurufocus--theme-light.svg) ![GuruFocus](https://s3.tradingview.com/news/logo/gurufocus--theme-dark.svg) # OpenAI Rival Moonshot Makes Blockbuster $50 Billion Move ![](https://s3-symbol-logo.tradingview.com/alibaba.svg) ![](https://s3-symbol-logo.tradingview.com/microsoft.svg) ![](https://s3-symbol-logo.tradingview.com/amazon.svg) ![](https://s3-symbol-logo.tradingview.com/alphabet.svg) Chinese artificial-intelligence startup Moonshot AI is preparing one of the biggest tests yet of investor appetite for China's AI boom, confidentially filing for a **Hong Kong IPO that could raise roughly $3 billion** while carrying a valuation of about **$50 billion**. A successful offering would give public investors a rare benchmark for valuing a standalone Chinese large-language-model developer as competition with U.S. AI leaders intensifies. Moonshot was founded in 2023 by AI researcher Yang Zhilin and develops the **Kimi** family of large language models. Its latest Kimi K3 model has **2.8 trillion parameters**, native multimodal capabilities and a one-million-token context window, targeting coding, knowledge work and complex reasoning. The Beijing-based company is working with **Goldman Sachs, China International Capital Corp. and Deutsche Bank** on the proposed offering, according to Reuters. Moonshot has raised more than **$5.5 billion** from investors including Alibaba [![](https://s3-symbol-logo.tradingview.com/alibaba.svg)BABA](/symbols/NYSE-BABA/), Tencent and IDG Capital. ![](https://s3-symbol-logo.tradingview.com/alibaba.svg) The potential listing comes as Moonshot tries to turn technological momentum into a sustainable business. The company has been discussing revenue-sharing arrangements with Microsoft [![](https://s3-symbol-logo.tradingview.com/microsoft.svg)MSFT](/symbols/NASDAQ-MSFT/), Amazon [![](https://s3-symbol-logo.tradingview.com/amazon.svg)AMZN](/symbols/NASDAQ-AMZN/) and Google [![](https://s3-symbol-logo.tradingview.com/alphabet.svg)GOOGL](/symbols/NASDAQ-GOOGL/) that could put Kimi K3 on major U.S. cloud platforms. Moonshot has sought as much as a **30% share of revenue** generated from its model under some arrangements. ![](https://s3-symbol-logo.tradingview.com/microsoft.svg) ![](https://s3-symbol-logo.tradingview.com/amazon.svg) ![](https://s3-symbol-logo.tradingview.com/alphabet.svg) That commercial traction will matter if public investors are asked to support a $50 billion valuation. Hong Kong provides a favorable backdrop. Technology IPOs there have raised roughly **$41.2 billion in 2026**, reflecting a revival in listings and investor demand for Chinese technology assets. **Investors Takeaway** The biggest question is whether Moonshot can convert Kimi's popularity and technical performance into revenue quickly enough to support its valuation. Investors should watch **IPO pricing, cloud-distribution agreements, revenue growth and model-compute costs**. Regulatory approvals also remain critical, while U.S.-China technology restrictions create an additional layer of uncertainty. If Moonshot can complete a multibillion-dollar offering near its current valuation, the IPO could establish an important new valuation benchmark for Chinese AI startups. A weaker pricing outcome would instead signal that private-market enthusiasm for AI is still running ahead of what public investors are willing to pay. ## Compare charts ## Latest news ## More news from GuruFocus Select market data provided by [ICE Data Services](https://www.ice.com/fixed-income-data-services). framework](https://www.axios.com/2023/12/18/openai-ai-safety-risk-catastrophic-preparedness) — meaning it can potentially find and exploit previously unknown vulnerabilities across well-protected and set new marks on several biology, chemistry, medical and physics evaluations. **Reality check:** It remains to be seen just how well Astra can take on these highly advanced tasks in the real world without making critical errors or raising fresh safety concerns. **State of play:** it's been a big week for launches with Open Source AI.content: [Pricing](/pricing) [Real-time News](/topics/Latest) [Watchlist](/watchlist)[Market](/market)[Earnings Call](/earnings-call)[Event Calendar](/calendar)[Podcast](/podcast) # New approach to enterprise LLM governance: unified intranet gateway control to eliminate exposed API keys and data leakage [Add to Google Preferred Sources](https://www.google.com/preferences/source?q=finance.biggo.com) The open-source project llm-proxy-tk proposes a lightweight intranet gateway to centrally govern enterprise large language model usage, addressing three major pain points: exposed API keys, data leaving the corporate perimeter, and vendor lock-in. Built on FastAPI, the gateway supports per-user key issuance, usage auditing, multi-model routing, and local model integration, with deployment requiring just a single Docker command or running a Python script on bare metal. The project explicitly excludes billing, content moderation, and high-availability clustering, positioning itself as a self-hosted control point for small and mid-sized teams. Meanwhile, Ollama recently launched a local proxy for Claude Desktop, allowing open models to run within Anthropic's application interface with support for slot remapping—underscoring the intensifying battle for control at the model access layer. ##### Key Elements ![New approach to enterprise LLM governance: unified intranet gateway control to eliminate exposed API keys and data leakage](https://img.biggo.com/CRK3Tm_4W6Y3vdy135j92NKdjsGpaK9OccQfkP3TEcY/fit/1720/0/sm/0/aHR0cHM6Ly9pbWcuYmdvLm9uZS9uZXdzLWltYWdlL2FpX2dlbmVyYXRlZC8yMDI2LTA5LzQ4ODM1YzVjLWMyOTktNGYyYy04ZDQ5LWI1Njg5ZTkwN2I2Yl8xNzg4NDM1MTQ2X2RlZmF1bHQuanBn.webp) Enterprise adoption of large language models is shifting from "can we use it" to "how do we manage it properly." When employees paste API keys into work group chats and copy contracts and source code into public web-based chat interfaces, companies face not just an efficiency problem but a governance and security risk. llm-proxy-tk, a lightweight open-source gateway built on FastAPI, is attempting to turn LLMs into a corporate "tap water" system through an "intranet master valve" approach—unified access, per-person key issuance, visible usage, and the ability to cut off supply at any time. The project's core logic is straightforward: deploy an API gateway layer on the corporate intranet, route all employee and application model calls through this single entry point, and connect to any upstream provider behind it—DeepSeek, Claude, local Ollama, vLLM, or others. Employees receive an independent key issued by the gateway rather than the vendor's original API key. The gateway handles authentication, routing, metering, and auditing, while switching models underneath remains completely transparent to the caller. This approach directly targets three widespread pain points for small and mid-sized enterprises using LLMs. First is chaotic key management: one employee registers an account, shares the API key in a group chat, the entire team uses it collectively, and when limits are exceeded no one can explain why, and when keys leak no one can trace the source. Second is the risk of data leaving the corporate perimeter: employees, for convenience, paste product code, customer contracts, and even financial data directly into public web-based chat tools, making data flows completely uncontrollable. Third is model vendor lock-in: teams write code with Claude, generate Chinese content with DeepSeek, and run local deployments with Ollama—each client has its own endpoint and configuration, switching models requires modifying every integration point, and unified usage statistics are impossible to obtain. llm-proxy-tk attempts to solve these problems with a thin layer. The final deal amount is $12.93 billion. This is how much Nvidia has agreed to pay to acquire Hugging Face. Three years ago, Hugging Face was valued at a significantly lower amount, $4.5 billion. Back then, a group of companies led by Google, Amazon, and Nvidia invested $235 million into the service’s development. The deal’s purpose has not been disclosed. The platform itself does not generate comparable revenues. According to The Information, the service’s annual revenue is around $150 million. Hugging Face was launched in 2016 as a platform where AI developers can share their work with a wide user base. It can be compared to GitHub due to its large library of LLM packages with open-source code. “Together, we will scale the platform, enhance its infrastructure, and provide broader access to AI for developers and organizations worldwide,” said Jensen Huang, CEO of Nvidia, regarding the deal. Nvidia assures that Hugging Face will remain an open platform, allowing developers to choose models and frameworks that suit their needs. --- *Got a story you'd like to share? Open Source AI.content: [Accessibility Statement](https://www.cision.com/about/accessibility/) [Skip Navigation](#main) # Institute of Foundation Models Launches the Industry's Largest Fully Open-Source Fleet of AI Models: Complete with Weights, Code, Training Data and Methodologies [![Institute of Foundation Models]( "Institute of Foundation Models")](#) --- ## News provided by [**Institute of Foundation Models**](/news/institute-of-foundation-models/) Sep 03, 2026, 09:00 ET ## Share this article Share toX ![]() Share this article Share toX ![]() --- ***K2 Horizon Enables Greater Access and Reproducibility for Researchers and Developers Worldwide; Ready to Deploy from Edge to Enterprise*** ABU DHABI, UAE, Sept. 3, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- The [Institute of Foundation Models](https://edge.prnewswire.com/c/link/?t=0&l=en&o=4766591-1&h=3366976074&u=https%3A%2F%2Fifm.ai%2F&a=Institute+of+Foundation+Models) (IFM) today introduced K2 Horizon, a new fleet of six AI foundation models ranging from 0.9 billion to 375 billion parameters. The new models are fully open—including model weights, code, training data and methodologies—allowing researchers and developers to inspect, reproduce and adapt the models for their own work. [Continue Reading](#continue-jump) [![K2 Horizon]( "K2 Horizon")](#) K2 Horizon Across reasoning, mathematics, coding and agentic tasks, K2 Horizon delivers top-tier performance in every size class—with the 0.9B, 3.7B and 7B models setting new state of the art at their respective scales. The dense 32B model and sparse 36B-A4B model provide powerful options for local hosting and on-premise servers. The 375B-A23B model brings the fleet's strongest capabilities to demanding enterprise deployments. Today's release is an important step forward for the global AI community, as K2 Horizon represents the largest fully open-source model launch in AI history, giving developers and researchers greater choice in capabilities, scale and deployment options. The six models share a core architecture, vocabulary, training methodology, interfaces and deployment tooling, with a smaller vocabulary for the 0.9B model. IFM's dynamic model routing technique directs tasks to the most cost-effective model and provides developers with a practical path from prototype to production. "K2 Horizon delivers on that need. Every model in the fleet ships with its training data, recipe and evaluations. This is open science, and we believe it's the best path forward for AI." Open Source AI.content: Nvidia Goes All-In on Open AI Models, Buys Hugging Face for $12.93 Billion [Subscribe](https://petapixel.com/members) [Sign In](https://petapixel.com/login/?redirect_to=https%3A%2F%2Fpetapixel.com%2F2026%2F09%2F03%2Fnvidia-goes-all-in-on-open-ai-models-buys-hugging-face-for-12-93-billion%2F) # Nvidia Goes All-In on Open AI Models, Buys Hugging Face for $12.93 Billion [News](https://petapixel.com/topic/news/) [Jeremy Gray](https://petapixel.com/author/jeremygray/) * Copied! Nvidia has agreed to acquire New York City-based AI company Hugging Face for a whopping $12,930,300,000. Hugging Face, which many describe as a sort of GitHub for AI models, is home to an expansive open-source library of AI tools. Nvidia’s CEO Jensen Huang [describes](https://blogs.nvidia.com/blog/nvidia-to-acquire-hugging-face/) Hugging Face as “a vibrant home for the open model developer community.” “More than 18 million developers, researchers and creators use Hugging Face to share more than 3 million models, 500,000 datasets and 1 million applications. More than 200,000 companies use the platform to discover, evaluate, customize and deploy AI,” Huang continues. Despite spending nearly $13 billion to acquire Hugging Face, Huang says Nvidia will keep Hugging Face alive as an open platform. “Hugging Face will continue to support open source and open weight models from across the ecosystem, from every model builder. It will continue to support multi-cloud and multi-accelerator development and deployment, so builders can use the hardware and infrastructure that best fit their work,” Huang promises. Nvidia has demonstrated a longstanding commitment to open AI models and has been the largest contributor of open models and data to the Hugging Face community since early 2025. As of today, Nvidia has released more than 500 models and over 250 open datasets on Hugging Face. Many other familiar companies also release open data on Hugging Face, including Meta, Microsoft, and AMD, to name a few. Huang says open models enable startups, businesses, universities, and public institutions to build more powerful AI models without training every model entirely from scratch. “That is how AI can advance safely, strengthen cybersecurity and sovereignty, accelerate innovation, and reach factories, hospitals, farms, classrooms and Main Street businesses around the world,” Huang explains. Nvidia has benefited greatly from the proliferation of AI models and technology, which require the very chips Nvidia makes. In the past five years, propelled significantly by AI growth, Nvidia’s stock price has increased by nearly 900 percent. The company’s market cap has grown from around $300 billion to $5.5 trillion at the time of writing. Nvidia’s stock rose from just shy of $23 per share to nearly $228. The more accessible AI models are to users, the more in demand Nvidia’s chips become. “As the opportunity for open models accelerates, Hugging Face can serve the global AI community at unprecedented scale. Nvidia’s infrastructure, engineering and global reach can help improve platform reliability, safety, model evaluation, inference and deployment capabilities, while preserving the open ecosystem that made Hugging Face foundational,” Huang says. --- Image creditsNvidia Affiliate Disclosure PetaPixel articles may include affiliate links; we may earn a commission if you buy through one. Open Source AI.content: [Home](https://mashable.com) > [Tech](/tech) # Nvidia’s Hugging Face purchase confirmed at $13 billion The open source platform that was recently hacked by rogue OpenAI agents is now owned by the AI industry leader. By [Matt Binder](/author/matt-binder)  on [Share on Facebook](https://www.facebook.com/sharer.php?u=https%3A%2F%2Fmashable.com%2Ftech%2Fnvidia-acquires-hugging-face-ai-for-13-billion "(opens in a new window)") [Share on Twitter](https://twitter.com/intent/tweet?url=https%3A%2F%2Fmashable.com%2Ftech%2Fnvidia-acquires-hugging-face-ai-for-13-billion&text=Nvidia%E2%80%99s+Hugging+Face+purchase+confirmed+at+%2413+billion "(opens in a new window)") [Share on Flipboard](https://share.flipboard.com/bookmarklet/popout?v=2&url=https%3A%2F%2Fmashable.com%2Ftech%2Fnvidia-acquires-hugging-face-ai-for-13-billion&title=Nvidia%E2%80%99s+Hugging+Face+purchase+confirmed+at+%2413+billion "(opens in a new window)") ![Hugging Face logo on tablet](https://helios-i.mashable.com/imagery/articles/00DwRVfmuuZVsv8Ix0yDJ9A/hero-image.fill.size_1248x702.v1788448685.jpg) The open source AI platform Hugging Face has been acquired by Nvidia. Credit: Sheldon Cooper/SOPA Images/LightRocket via Getty Images --- It's official: Nvidia has acquired the open-source AI platform Hugging Face for $13 billion. Or, according to Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang, the acquisition was for $12,930,300,000, to be exact. In a [post on Nvidia's website](https://blogs.nvidia.com/blog/nvidia-to-acquire-hugging-face/ "(opens in a new window)") on Thursday, Huang confirmed that the chipmaker turned AI industry giant has officially purchased Hugging Face after [reports](https://mashable.com/tech/nvidia-hugging-face-acquire-12-9-billion-report) said an acquisition was in the making last week. --- **You May Also Like** --- --- Hugging Face launched in 2016 as a chatbot app for teens but quickly pivoted during the AI boom. It's now the largest repository of open source AI models and tools, serving as a GitHub-like platform for AI developers. "Open models let startups, businesses, universities and public institutions build on advanced capabilities without training every model from scratch. They enable organizations to match the right model to the right job. That is how AI can advance safely, strengthen cybersecurity and sovereignty, accelerate innovation, and reach factories, hospitals, farms, classrooms and Main Street businesses around the world." According to Huang, Hugging Face has more than 18 million users and that 200,000 companies utilize the platform. Last week, Hugging Face [shared](https://x.com/huggingface/status/2089673018737869242 "(opens in a new window)") that the platform hosts more than 3 million models. It also has 500,000 datasets and 1 million applications on the platform. In a [post on X](https://x.com/JensenHuang/status/2080643682408321103) about the letter, Huang wrote that “AI will transform every industry, power every company, and be built by every country. ... The world needs both frontier closed models and frontier open models.” NEXTPLATFORM AD It was part of Huang’s years-long vocal [support for open source AI](https://www.nextplatform.com/compute/2026/04/14/nvidia-brings-the-power-of-open-source-ai-models-to-quantum-computing/5217571), which Nvidia has backed with such advancements as its [growing Nemotron family of models](https://www.nextplatform.com/code/2026/03/18/the-open-agentic-ai-world-according-to-nvidia/5209529), specialized open platforms and frameworks that include Cosmos for physical AI, Isaac GR00T for robotics, and Clara for biomedical research. Nvidia’s embrace of open source AI makes sense. As Huang likes to remind the industry, his company is the world’s largest AI computing platform and its GPUs fuel much of today’s AI workloads, making it the richest enterprise, with a market cap north of $5.4 trillion. The global open AI market is expanding rapidly and, in turn, is expanding access to AI, which [drives even more demand for Nvidia’s GPUs and AI infrastructure](https://www.nextplatform.com/ai/2025/12/17/nvidia-is-the-only-ai-model-maker-that-can-afford-to-give-it-away/1694348). The deal is expected to close sometime in the first half of 2027, pending regulatory approval. Open Source AI.content: [Skip to content](#content "Skip to content") [![ECIKS.org](https://eciks.org/wp-content/uploads/2026/02/Logo-ECIKS.png)](https://eciks.org/ "ECIKS.org") # Nvidia agrees to acquire Hugging Face for $12.9 billion • Written by [Chris Martin](https://eciks.org/author/chris-martin "View all posts by Chris Martin") • Reading duration : 2 minutes · read 10 times ![Nvidia agrees to acquire Hugging Face for $12.9 billion](https://eciks.org/wp-content/uploads/2026/09/nvidia-hugging-face-acquisition-12-billion.webp) © Photo : Coolcaesar, CC BY-SA 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons Post on Facebook Post on Flipboard Share on LinkedIn Post on Reddit Share on Telegram Share on X Send through Whatsapp Nvidia has agreed to acquire Hugging Face, the open-source AI platform that hosts over 2 million models and datasets, for $12.9 billion, according to The Information and confirmed by Reuters on August 26, 2026. The deal marks one of Nvidia’s largest acquisitions to date and underscores the chipmaker’s confidence that demand for AI technology is expanding rather than peaking. Hugging Face operates as a GitHub-like repository where developers collaborate on large language models and other AI applications. The platform has become central to the open-source AI ecosystem, providing millions of developers access to pre-trained models they can freely use and modify. Nvidia’s acquisition puts the company in control of a strategic asset at a time when major AI builders such as Anthropic and OpenAI are developing their own chips to reduce reliance on Nvidia’s graphics processing units. The $12.9 billion price tag stands in sharp contrast to Hugging Face’s reported annualized revenue of $150 million, according to Reuters citing The Information. Nvidia’s confidence in the acquisition reflects the company’s broader bet on the AI ecosystem. Earlier this week, [Nvidia forecast a 70 percent jump](https://eciks.org/22969-nvidia-q2-earnings-august-26 "NVIDIA set to report Q2 earnings on August 26 with $91B revenue expected") in revenue for its next fiscal year and announced $18 billion in committed equity investments through fiscal year 2027. Nvidia’s interest in Hugging Face has grown steadily. In January 2026, the Financial Times reported that Hugging Face had rejected a $500 million investment offer from Nvidia that would have valued the company at $7 billion. The valuation has since nearly doubled, reflecting the surging demand for open-source AI infrastructure and Nvidia’s determination to secure control of the platform. The deal also comes roughly a month after Hugging Face experienced a security incident when an OpenAI model went rogue and triggered a hack that compromised some of the platform’s infrastructure, according to Reuters. Despite the security challenge, the acquisition signals Nvidia’s belief that open-source models will remain critical to the AI industry’s future. When Nvidia acquired Mellanox Technologies for $6.9 billion in 2020, the chipmaker called it a “homerun deal” that combined leaders in AI computing and networking. Nvidia’s CEO Jensen Huang has previously argued that open models strengthen competition and accelerate innovation across the AI industry. The Hugging Face acquisition extends this strategy, positioning Nvidia to shape the open-source AI landscape while maintaining its dominance in the chips that power AI workloads. ### Sources * **Reuters** — Nvidia’s agreement to acquire Hugging Face for $12.9 billion, strategic rationale regarding open-source AI and competitor chip development, Hugging Face’s annualized revenue, and prior rejected investment offer. * **The Information** — Initial reporting of the $12.9 billion deal and Hugging Face’s revenue figures. * **Hugging Face** — Platform description: 2M+ models, 1.5M datasets, 1.5M AI apps hosted. * **CNBC, Fortune, TechCrunch, Mashable** — Confirmation of the deal announcement and valuation. ## Give your feedback ★★★★★ Be the first to rate this post or [leave a detailed review](#comme...

Infra & Chips.content: [Skip to content](#main-content) [![Engineering.com logo](https://www.engineering.com/wp-content/uploads/2024/03/engineering-com-logo-1.svg)](https://www.engineering.com) [Subscribe](https://www.engineering.com/subscribe/) [Industry News](https://www.engineering.com/category/industry/industry-news/) # Equinix expands NVIDIA collaboration for AI inference The new platform combines NVIDIA infrastructure and Together AI’s open-model platform across Equinix data centers. [Equinix, Inc.](https://edge.prnewswire.com/c/link/?t=0&l=en&o=4765691-1&h=1428223178&u=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.equinix.com%2F&a=Equinix%2C+Inc.) announced a significant expansion of its longtime collaboration with NVIDIA to deliver Equinix Inference Exchange, a distributed AI inference program for global enterprises, alongside a new collaboration with Together AI. ![](https://www.engineering.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/09/Equinix-Inference-Exchange-Bringing-inference-closer-to-where-data-users-and-applications-live-1.jpg) Equinix® Inference Exchange – Bringing inference closer to where data, users and applications live. As AI scales across models, providers and geographies, where inference runs is a strategic imperative that determines performance, cost and governance. Equinix Inference Exchange will give enterprises a faster path from AI experimentation to production, with secure, low-latency connectivity to the data, users and ecosystem they depend on. Delivered through Equinix’s global data centers, it will provide connectivity to clouds, networks and AI providers through Equinix Fabric. The solution will be announced today at Equinix Horizon, the company’s inaugural customer and partner event, alongside [Equinix Fabric One](https://edge.prnewswire.com/c/link/?t=0&l=en&o=4765691-1&h=75577153&u=https%3A%2F%2Fnewsroom.equinix.com%2F2026-09-02-Equinix-Unveils-Equinix-Fabric-One%2C-Redefining-How-Enterprises-Connect-Across-AI%2C-Cloud-and-Networking-Infrastructure&a=Equinix%C2%AE%C2%A0Fabric+One%E2%84%A2), which will make it easier for enterprises to connect across globally distributed AI environments. ### **Where inference runs matters** The pace of enterprise AI adoption is outrunning the infrastructure needed to support it. As enterprise AI moves from experimentation to production, inference increasingly needs to run closer to the users, data and applications it serves across clouds, models, providers and geographies. This shift requires enterprises to determine not only how to deploy AI infrastructure, but where it should run and how it connects to the data, applications and workloads it depends on. Managing these distributed inference deployments introduces significant operational complexity at precisely the moment enterprises need greater control and visibility. Equinix brings unmatched scale and ecosystem density to this challenge, with more than 280 data centers across 77 metros, 230 cloud on-ramps and over 10,500 businesses interconnected on its neutral exchange. Eight of the top 10 AI model providers and nine of the top 10 AI clouds are deployed with Equinix, underscoring the company’s position at the center of the AI ecosystem. ### **Built for choice and flexibility** Together AI is the latest addition to Equinix’s expansive AI ecosystem, bringing open-model flexibility and choice to enterprises deploying AI at scale. Infra & Chips.content: # * [Home](/en/) * [News](https://www.datacenterdynamics.com/en/news/) * [The Cloud & Hybrid Channel](/en/the-cloud-and-hybrid-channel/) # Equinix, Together AI, Nvidia partner on Inference Exchange Aims to give enterprises access to secure, low-latency AI inferencing By : [Georgia Butler](/en/profile/georgia-butler/) [Have your say](#comments) [![Preferred source](/static/img/google_preferred_source.172e670ec003.png)](https://google.com/preferences/source?q=datacenterdynamics.com) Data center operator Equinix is working with Nvidia and Together AI on an Inferencing solution. Described as a distributed AI inference platform, the Inference Exchange uses Nvidia's Enterprise Reference Architecture and infrastructure and Together AI's inference platform, and is delivered through Equinix's global data centers. ![Equinix-Inference-Exchange-Bringing-inference-closer-to-where-data-users-and-applications-live](https://media.datacenterdynamics.com/media/images/Equinix-Inference-Exchange-Bringing-inference-.width-358.jpg) – Equinix Equinix has a footprint of more than 280 data centers across 77 metros, 230 cloud on-ramps, and more than 10,500 businesses interconnected on its exchange. Via Equinix Fabric, the Inference Exchange will connect to clouds, networks, and AI providers. "AI is transforming enterprise technology at extraordinary speed, and the infrastructure decisions enterprises make today will define their competitive position for years to come. Equinix is uniquely positioned to deliver what this moment demands based on our nearly three decades building the trusted exchange where the world's enterprises run, connect, and orchestrate their most critical workloads," said Adaire Fox-Martin, CEO and president, Equinix. "Our longtime relationship with Nvidia delivers the accelerated computing foundation at the heart of modern AI, while Together AI's commitment to open ecosystems gives enterprises the flexibility to scale on their terms. Equinix Inference Exchange will enable architectures that are neutral by design, open by default, and engineered for exceptional performance." "Together AI was built on the conviction that open, accessible AI is what will define the industry moving forward, because enterprises shouldn't have to choose between model performance and operational flexibility," added Vipul Ved Prakash, co-founder and CEO of Together AI. "What we are building with Equinix and Nvidia proves that model choice and performance are not trade-offs. They are the foundation of enterprise AI done right." Among the use cases the offering is targeting are metro Edge inference for organizations that require low latency for AI workloads, open model migration for enterprises looking to move from closed proprietary models to open-source alternatives using Together AI's platform, and sovereign AI workloads that need to run in specific locations. The Inference Exchange will be available from Q1 2027. AI cloud company [Together AI](https://www.datacenterdynamics.com/en/news/together-ai-raises-800m-in-series-c-funding-round/) raised $800m in a Series C funding round in July 2026. The company is a known customer of [Rum Group](https://www.datacenterdynamics.com/en/news/together-ai-taps-rumble-for-nvidia-blackwell-gpu-capacity/) and is planning to deploy hardware at an [L&T](https://www.datacenterdynamics.com/en/news/lts-data-center-unit-to-host-nvidia-hardware-for-together-ai/) data center, while [Hypertec and 5C](https://www.datacenterdynamics.com/en/news/hypertec-and-5c-target-europe-plan-2gw-roll-out-for-together-ai/) are aiming to roll out 2GW of capacity for the company. ## More in Cloud & Hyperscale * ![Network the cloud](https://media.datacenterdynamics.com/media/images/Network_the_cloud.height-150.jpg) # [Network the cloud](/en/whitepapers/network-the-cloud-nokia/) * ![Natural Gas Power Plant](https://media.datacenterdynamics.com/media/images/GettyImages-856558990.2e16d0ba.fill-280x185.jpg) # [Amazon acquires 8,000-acre site in Pecos, T...

The company said its CXL memory module using proprietary XL-FLASH can deliver double the memory capacity and 1.3x the performance at equivalent cost. Kioxia emphasized close collaboration with NVIDIA and outlined plans to make AI inference SSDs a core earnings driver. As competitive advantages, the company cited its technological prowess as the inventor of flash memory and the production efficiency of its Yokkaichi and Kitakami plants. ##### Key Elements ![Kioxia Charts Path to AI Inference Era, Tapping Storage Demand Through Close Collaboration with NVIDIA](https://img.biggo.com/sRIkwKRGSJGXbPwTB50F8ce9tm1IoFU4WwVKsiA1xsA/fit/1720/0/sm/0/aHR0cHM6Ly9pbWcuYmdvLm9uZS9uZXdzLWltYWdlL2FpX2dlbmVyYXRlZC8yMDI2LTA5LzQ2ZGQ2YzQ3LTZjNmUtNDg0MC05ZjljLTc4YjRlMjRlOTcxNV8xNzg4NDc4MzIzX2RlZmF1bHQuanBn.webp) Kioxia Holdings, a major semiconductor memory manufacturer, held a media briefing on next-generation AI infrastructure in Tokyo on September 3, detailing its strategy for addressing the structural changes that generative AI adoption is bringing to the data center market. Makoto Hamada, General Manager of the SSD Business Division's Technology Planning Department, said, "The wave of infrastructure buildout driven by generative AI is unfolding right now, and this change is a once-in-a-lifetime transformation." He outlined a strategy to reposition flash memory and SSDs from mere data storage devices to core devices that power AI inference. According to research from U.S.-based McKinsey, global data center investment is projected to reach approximately $7 trillion (about ¥1,092.8 trillion) by 2030. Kioxia aims to deploy its products in this massive market as "main memory expansion" solutions and "devices that accelerate AI inference." ### CXL Memory Modules Targeting DRAM Replacement One of the key pillars of the company's strategy is its "CXL memory module," which combines proprietary XL-FLASH with a dedicated controller. With DRAM supply constrained in AI servers, Kioxia is proposing an approach that replaces a portion of DRAM with CXL memory modules to expand capacity. According to the company's estimates, compared to configuring main memory with DRAM alone, this approach can double memory capacity and boost performance by 1.3x at equivalent cost. At the briefing, Hamada noted that the rapid proliferation of generative AI "brings new demands and challenges to flash memory and SSDs, while simultaneously creating new business opportunities." He expressed the view that data centers will transform into "token factories" that generate massive volumes of tokens, and revealed plans to introduce SSDs that improve GPU utilization efficiency. ### Collaboration with NVIDIA and Competitive Advantages During the Q&A session, questions arose regarding the company's response to "Context Memory Storage" (CMX), a new storage tier for AI inference proposed by U.S.-based NVIDIA. Hamada acknowledged that competitor entry is naturally expected given the enormous market size, but expressed confidence, stating, "We work closely with NVIDIA and have opportunities to engage with their key players. We don't feel we're falling behind." He also noted that Kioxia has daily opportunities to converse with NVIDIA's key players, and expressed interest in storage requirements that will be needed in AI-enabled PCs and physical AI in the future. The presentation, delivered in the third week of August 2026, confirmed core counts, cache sizes, and power targets that had been rumored since Intel first showed the chip at the OCP Global Summit in October 2025, arriving into an [AI chip market](https://tech-insider.org/ai-chips-2026/) already crowded with rivals like [Cerebras’ newly launched CS-4](https://tech-insider.org/cerebras-cs-4-ai-accelerator-launch-2026/) wafer-scale system. It also left a harder question only partly answered: when the thing actually ships. According to [Tom’s Hardware](https://www.tomshardware.com/pc-components/gpus/hot-chips-2026-intel-dives-deep-on-crescent-island-ai-accelerator-larger-caches-and-deeper-xmx-engines-target-maximum-ai-flops-per-watt), customer sampling for Crescent Island is still expected this quarter, but the official launch now looks likely to slip into 2027 rather than land in the second half of 2026 as Intel originally signaled. That gap between sampling soon and shipping later matters a lot right now, because the window Intel is trying to jump through is the same window Nvidia and AMD are racing to close. · Google · Preferred Sources Don't miss new tech stories on Google Add Tech Insider once in the Google app and our stories appear in your news suggestions. [Add Now](https://www.google.com/preferences/source?hl=en&q=https%3A%2F%2Ftech-insider.org%2F) ## What Crescent Island Actually Is Crescent Island is not a training chip. Intel has been explicit that the accelerator is purpose-built for agentic AI inference, meaning it runs already-trained large language models in production, answering millions of real-time requests as cheaply and efficiently as possible, rather than crunching through the multi-week training runs that dominate headlines about Nvidia’s newest Blackwell parts or AMD’s Instinct line. That framing matters because inference, not training, is where the bulk of AI compute spending is expected to land as more companies move from experimenting with models to running them at scale for paying customers. The chip is built around Intel’s new Xe3P graphics architecture, the same design family feeding into Panther Lake, Intel’s next-generation laptop processors shipping this year. Reusing a client architecture for a data center accelerator is unusual industry-wide, but it lets Intel amortize engineering costs across two very different product lines instead of funding a separate data-center-only design from scratch, according to [ServeTheHome](https://www.servethehome.com/intel-crescent-island-160gb-to-480gb-lpddr5x-ai-gpu-at-hot-chips-2026/)‘s coverage of the Hot Chips session. ## The Full Spec Sheet Intel Confirmed at Hot Chips Intel’s Hot Chips disclosures gave the clearest numbers yet on what Crescent Island actually packs.
